너.forms: subject: 네가 (spoken 니가) · object: 너를 · your: 네 (네 책)
너.x: My friend asked, 'Where are you right now?'
너.e: Becomes 네가 before 가 — usually pronounced 니가 so it doesn't sound like 내가 (I).
너.t: Only for close friends your age or younger people. With others, use their name or title instead of 'you'.

눈.x: That child has really big eyes.
눈.t: 눈 also means 'snow'; in careful speech 'snow' has a long vowel [눈ː].

눈.e: Snow is said with a longer vowel.
눈.t: 눈 also means 'eye'. Context tells them apart: 눈이 와요 (it snows) vs 눈이 아파요 (my eyes hurt).

절.ex: 산속에 있는 조용한 절에서 하룻밤을 보냈어요.
절.x: I spent a night at a quiet temple in the mountains.
절.e: Homonym warning: 절 also means 'a deep bow' (절하다).
절.t: Temple names end in Sino-Korean -사 'temple': 불국사, 해인사, 조계사.

절.x: On Lunar New Year's morning, I bowed to my parents.
절.e: Homonym warning: 절 also means 'Buddhist temple', so check the context.

돌아다니다.m: to walk around, to wander, to get around
돌아다니다.ex: 하루 종일 시내를 돌아다녀서 다리가 아파요.
돌아다니다.x: I walked around downtown all day, so my legs hurt.
돌아다니다.e: 돌다 'to turn' + 다니다 'to go around': moving from place to place.

젖다.m: to get wet, to be wet
젖다.x: I didn't have an umbrella, so my clothes got completely wet.
젖다.e: Opposite pair: 젖다 (get wet) and 마르다 (get dry).
젖다.t: Usually used in the past tense for a current state: 옷이 젖었어요 = my clothes are wet.

초.ex: 이 문제는 삼십 초 안에 풀어야 해요.
초.x: You have to solve this problem within thirty seconds.
초.e: Homonym warning: other 초 words mean 'candle' and 'beginning (of a period)'.
초.t: Seconds use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 초, 삼십 초.

갖다.forms: 가져요 · 가졌어요 · 가질 거예요 · 가지세요 (short form of 가지다; vowel endings use 가지-)
갖다.m: to have, to own, to hold
갖다.ex: 저는 어릴 때부터 음악에 관심을 갖고 있었어요.
갖다.x: I have been interested in music since I was little.
갖다.e: Contracted from 가지다; the short form only joins consonant endings like -고, -는.
갖다.t: In speech 갖다 주다 means 'to bring something to someone': 물 좀 갖다 주세요.

심하다.m: to be severe, to be serious; to be too much, harsh
심하다.ex: 감기가 심해서 오늘 학교에 못 갔어요.
심하다.x: My cold was bad, so I couldn't go to school today.

꾸준히.x: If you study consistently every day, your skills will improve.
꾸준히.e: Adverb form of 꾸준하다 (to be steady).

예.ex: 선생님이 이해하기 쉬운 예를 하나 들어 주셨어요.
예.x: The teacher gave us an example that was easy to understand.
예.e: Best learned in the set phrase 예를 들면, 'for example'.
예.t: Don't confuse it with 예 meaning 'yes'; to give an example is 예를 들다.

경력.ex: 이 일은 경력이 삼 년 이상 필요해요.
경력.x: This job requires at least three years of experience.
경력.t: Pronounced [경녁] — ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

뼈.x: I fell on the stairs and broke a bone in my arm.
뼈.e: Also found in 갈비뼈 'rib' and 뼈다귀 'a bone' (casual).

어기다.m: to break (a rule, promise, law), to violate
어기다.ex: 친구가 또 약속을 어겨서 화가 났어요.
어기다.x: I got angry because my friend broke a promise again.
어기다.t: The opposite is 지키다: 약속을 지키다 'keep a promise' vs. 약속을 어기다 'break a promise.'

거래처.x: I have a meeting with someone from a client company this afternoon.
거래처.e: Literally 'place you go back and forth with', i.e., trade with.

경쟁하다.ex: 두 회사가 새 시장에서 경쟁하고 있어요.
경쟁하다.x: The two companies are competing in a new market.

냉방.ex: 지하철 안은 냉방이 잘 되어서 시원해요.
냉방.x: The subway is well air-conditioned, so it's cool.
냉방.e: Literally 'cold room'; the opposite is 난방 'heating'.
냉방.t: 냉방병 is a common Korean term for colds or fatigue blamed on strong air conditioning.

말다툼.x: I had an argument with my younger sibling yesterday.
말다툼.e: 말 'words' + 다툼 'quarrel': a fight with words only.

친환경적.x: Bicycles are an eco-friendly means of transportation with no exhaust fumes.
친환경적.e: 친환경 'eco-friendly' + -적; used as an adjective with 인 or 으로.

쌈.ex: 상추에 고기를 올려서 쌈을 싸 먹어요.
쌈.x: I put meat on lettuce, wrap it up and eat it.
쌈.t: 'Make a wrap' is 쌈을 싸다. Make it bite-sized and eat it in one mouthful.

통증.x: If you have back pain, don't overdo it.
통증.t: 통증 is physical, medical pain; 고통 also covers emotional suffering.

용량.x: My phone was low on storage, so I deleted some photos.
용량.t: Pronounced [용냥]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

긍정.ex: 그는 제 질문에 고개를 끄덕여 긍정했어요.
긍정.x: He nodded to say yes to my question.
긍정.e: Literally 'affirm and settle' — saying yes to something.
긍정.t: For a 'positive' attitude, Koreans use 긍정적: 긍정적인 사람 'a positive person'.

비틀다.forms: 비틀어요 · 비틀었어요 · 비틀 거예요 · 비트세요 (ㄹ drops)
비틀다.x: I wrung out the wet towel.

풍족하다.ex: 어릴 때 집이 풍족하지 않았지만 행복했어요.
풍족하다.x: We weren't well-off when I was a kid, but I was happy.
풍족하다.t: Pronounced [풍조카다]. Often about money and living conditions; 풍부하다 suits resources and knowledge.

입이 짧다.m: to be a picky eater, to eat very little
입이 짧다.ex: 우리 아들은 입이 짧아서 밥을 조금만 먹어요.
입이 짧다.x: My son is a picky eater, so he only eats a little.
입이 짧다.e: Literally 'a short mouth'; it's about eating, not talking.
입이 짧다.t: Pronounced [이비 짤따]: in 짧다 the ㄼ sounds like ㄹ.

혀를 차다.forms: 혀를 차요 · 혀를 찼어요 · 쯧쯧 (the sound)
혀를 차다.m: to click one's tongue (in disapproval or pity)
혀를 차다.x: Grandpa clicked his tongue as he watched the news.
혀를 차다.e: The click itself is written 쯧쯧, Korean for 'tsk-tsk.'

환절기.x: It's easy to catch a cold when the seasons change.
환절기.t: 환절기 감기 조심하세요 'watch out for colds at the change of season' is a common caring remark; the big gap between day and night temperatures gets the blame.

통신망.ex: 한국은 전국에 빠른 통신망이 깔려 있어요.
통신망.x: Korea has fast communication networks installed across the country.

얼마간.m: for a while, for some time; somewhat, to some extent
얼마간.ex: 퇴원한 후에도 얼마간 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
얼마간.x: Even after leaving the hospital, you need to rest at home for a while.
얼마간.e: From 얼마 'how much' + 간 'span': some amount of time or degree.

워라밸.ex: 요즘 젊은 직장인들은 연봉보다 워라밸을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
워라밸.x: These days young office workers value work-life balance more than salary.
워라밸.e: Shortened from English 'work-life balance' — a Korean-made clipping.
워라밸.t: Casual and trendy; in formal writing use 일과 삶의 균형.

수채화.ex: 저는 주말마다 공원에 가서 수채화를 그려요.
수채화.x: Every weekend I go to the park and paint watercolors.

꼼꼼히.ex: 계약서에 서명하기 전에 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요.
꼼꼼히.x: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.
꼼꼼히.t: Its opposite in daily speech is 대충 (roughly, half-heartedly).

시말서.m: written explanation and apology for a mistake (at work)
시말서.ex: 무단 결근을 해서 회사에 시말서를 썼어요.
시말서.x: I skipped work without notice, so I had to write a letter of apology to the company.
시말서.e: Literally 'beginning-to-end document' — a full account of a mistake, from start to finish.
시말서.t: Writing a 시말서 is a formal workplace disciplinary step; many companies now prefer the term 경위서.

작정하다.m: to make up one's mind, to be determined to, to intend
작정하다.x: I made up my mind to quit smoking this year for sure.
작정하다.t: 작정하고 means 'deliberately, on purpose': 작정하고 놀았어요 (I partied with full intent).

가심비.m: satisfaction for the price, worth it for how it makes you feel
가심비.ex: 좀 비싸도 가심비가 좋으면 사는 편이에요.
가심비.x: Even if it's a bit pricey, I tend to buy it if it's worth it for how it makes me feel.
가심비.e: Short for 가격 대비 심리적 만족 'psychological satisfaction relative to price', modeled on 가성비.
가심비.t: A trend word from around 2018: spending more on things that make you happy, even if they aren't the best value.

필리버스터.ex: 야당 의원들이 법안을 막으려고 필리버스터를 시작했습니다.
필리버스터.x: Opposition lawmakers started a filibuster to block the bill.
필리버스터.e: From English 'filibuster'; officially called 무제한 토론 in Korea's National Assembly.

괴리감.m: sense of disconnect, gap between expectation and reality
괴리감.ex: 이상과 현실 사이에서 괴리감을 느낄 때가 많아요.
괴리감.x: I often feel a gap between my ideals and reality.
괴리감.t: Common pattern: A와 B 사이의 괴리감 — the gap between A and B.

대조군.ex: 연구팀은 대조군에게 진짜 약 대신 가짜 약을 주었습니다.
대조군.x: The research team gave the control group a fake pill instead of the real medicine.

방화벽.ex: 방화벽을 설정하면 외부의 공격을 막을 수 있어요.
방화벽.x: Setting up a firewall can block outside attacks.
방화벽.e: Literally 'wall that prevents fire' — first a building term, then a computer one.
방화벽.t: Don't confuse 방화 'fire prevention' with its homonym 방화 'arson'.

영탄법.ex: '아, 아름다운 우리 강산이여!'는 영탄법이 쓰인 구절이에요.
영탄법.x: 'Ah, our beautiful land!' is a line that uses exclamation.
영탄법.e: Literally 'chant-sigh method' — expressing strong feeling with 아, 오 or -여.

추임새.m: chuimsae, shouts of encouragement during a performance (like 얼씨구, 좋다)
추임새.x: The audience shouted 'Eolssigu!' to cheer the performer on.
추임새.e: Probably related to 추어올리다 'to praise, to cheer up'.
추임새.t: The verb is 넣다: 추임새를 넣다; it's also used casually for chiming in to cheer a speaker.

악용하다.m: to abuse, to misuse, to exploit (for bad ends)
악용하다.ex: 개인 정보를 악용하는 범죄가 늘고 있습니다.
악용하다.x: Crimes that misuse personal information are increasing.

응징하다.m: to punish, to chastise, to retaliate against
응징하다.ex: 정부는 테러 세력을 강력히 응징하겠다고 밝혔습니다.
응징하다.x: The government vowed to punish the terrorist groups severely.

엘리트주의.ex: 그 정치인은 엘리트주의적인 태도로 비판을 받았습니다.
엘리트주의.x: The politician was criticized for his elitist attitude.
엘리트주의.e: From English 'elite' + -주의 '-ism', a highly productive suffix: 개인주의, 민주주의.
엘리트주의.t: Pronounced [엘리트주이]; add -적 for the adjective: 엘리트주의적인 태도.

해수면 상승.ex: 해수면 상승으로 섬나라들이 사라질 위기에 놓였습니다.
해수면 상승.x: Island nations are in danger of disappearing because of sea-level rise.

낭랑하다.x: The child read the poem in a clear, ringing voice.
낭랑하다.e: Literally 'bright, bright' — a voice as clear as light.
낭랑하다.t: Pronounced [낭낭하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

번연히.x: He knew full well, yet pretended not to know.
번연히.t: Most common in 번연히 알면서(도) 'even while knowing full well'.

역학관계.ex: 최근 두 나라의 역학관계가 크게 변했습니다.
역학관계.x: The power dynamics between the two countries have changed greatly recently.

조세피난처.x: Some companies hid money in tax havens.
조세피난처.e: Literally 'tax + refuge place': a shelter where money escapes taxes.
